gen-gf-chiron-goround-tc-fs-literata: Rounded, friendly strokes with no fuss define Chiron GoRound TC, and its low contrast feels approachable and current. Literata, a text serif, adds a bookish, sturdy voice beneath.
gen-gf-chiron-hei-hk-fs-literata: Chiron Hei HK keeps every curve end open and its stroke weight barely modulated, which feels modern and friendly. Literata's thicker and thinner lines then give the text a bookish, steady pace.
gen-gf-chiron-sung-hk-fs-bespoke-sans: Literary and editorial, Chiron Sung HK shifts gently from thick to thin so its rounded letters feel alive. And Bespoke Sans, sharp and low in contrast, lets paragraphs move along cleanly with generous space at its curve ends.
gen-gf-cinzel-fs-bespoke-sans: Carved, ceremonial capitals with a sigh of space after each one: that is Cinzel, traditional and authoritative. Bespoke Sans, a plain sans, takes over with sharp, refined lines and generous room where curves meet stems, so long text stays easy on the eye.
gen-gf-commissioner-fs-literata: Literata brings a bookish, sophisticated voice, with curves that thicken gently at the shoulders and wide, unclosed mouths. Commissioner's thin, technical-pen line sits above it, so choose a body size that lets those curves breathe.
gen-gf-crimson-text-fs-bespoke-sans: Compact, bookish, and quietly classic. Crimson Text packs its words tight with sturdy hairlines and open curves, while Bespoke Sans, a plain sans, is sharper and refined, with low contrast and generous space around every curve end.
gen-gf-cuprum-fs-literata: Tight, tucked-together letters with a modern, approachable edge. Cuprum is best at compact, confident headings with strokes between monoline and contrasted, while Literata, a serif, is best at sturdy, bookish text with wide, unclosed curves.
gen-gf-cutive-mono-fs-literata: Cutive Mono is precise and technical, with typewriter-width letters and an s you can see straight through. Literata, a classic serif, then adds thick strokes that lead the eye without dominating it, so a larger heading than body size feels natural.
gen-gf-dai-banna-sil-fs-bespoke-sans: Editorial and classic, Dai Banna SIL sets its letters nearly shoulder to shoulder, with open curves and modest stress. But Bespoke Sans, a plain sans, reads sharp and refined over a longer stretch, thanks to low contrast and generous space at its curve ends.
gen-gf-datatype-fs-literata: Datatype is structured and precise, with a gaping c and bent-tubing strokes. Its best trick is a constant marker-like line in typewriter widths, while Literata, a text serif, does the bookish, sophisticated reading with moderately contrasting strokes.
